data.text:
On May 2, 2026, more than 80 years after his death in WWII, Medal of Honor Recipient Army Capt. Willibald C. Bianchi was finally brought home and laid to rest alongside his family in his hometown of New Ulm, Minnesota.

A Soldier of extraordinary courage, Bianchi repeatedly exposed himself to enemy fire during the Battle of Bataan, continuing to lead and fight even after being severely wounded multiple times.

After the fall of the Philippines, he endured the horrors of the Bataan Death March and years as a prisoner of w@r, continually caring for and encouraging fellow prisoners in the darkest of conditions.

In 2025, the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency identified his remains more than eight decades after his death aboard the Enoura Maru in January 1945.

His story is a reminder that service, sacrifice, and courage are never forgotten. We honor Capt. Blanchi and all those still unaccounted for who gave so much in defense of our nation.

#SciFeature 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗨𝗦𝗬 𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗠𝗘 𝗥𝗢𝗨𝗧𝗘𝗦 🚢

The global oil crisis intensified when the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran, was effectively “closed” amid ongoing conflict. As a critical maritime choke point, it handles roughly 20% of the world’s oil supply, making disruptions globally significant.

In the Philippines, we also rely on busy sea lanes and strategic “choke points,” where trade and maritime traffic converge, making them equally vital and vulnerable.

Here’s a map visualizing the bustling shipping routes within and surrounding the Philippine archipelago, transporting passengers and goods to and from the ports across the country. 

From ancient balangays to modern-day ferries and cargo ships, sea transport has always been the lifeblood connecting communities across our 7,000+ islands. Today, thousands of vessels navigate these waters daily, carrying passengers and goods that power our economy and link our lives.

This map shows the total AIS (Automatic Identification System) positions reported by commercial, fishing, oil & gas, passenger, and leisure vessels over a 6-year period, giving us a stunning view of both major and lesser-known maritime highways across the country. Notice how the Port of Manila stands out as the busiest hub, with vibrant routes also extending to and from key cities like Batangas, Cebu, and Cagayan de Oro. #OceanMonth
